questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Vanuatu?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Vanuatu article.

questions.proof: The capital of Vanuatu is Port Vila.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Vanuatu?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Vanuatu article.

questions.proof: The official languages of Vanuatu are Bislama, English and French.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The country was ruled as a colony by England and _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “England”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Vanuatu article.

questions.proof: The country was ruled as a colony by England and France.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “This is because of the island chain's closeness to the Solomon Islands and New _____, where crocodiles are very common.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “crocodiles”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Vanuatu article, under the heading “Flora and fauna”.

questions.proof: This is because of the island chain's closeness to the Solomon Islands and New Guinea, where crocodiles are very common.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Evidence shows, that people lived in Vanuatu by _____ BC.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the thirteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Vanuatu article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: Evidence shows, that people lived in Vanuatu by 1300 BC.
